before.known: why do you want to learn Arabic so soon?
before.target: لِماذا تُريدُ أَنْ تَتَعَلَّمَ العَرَبِيَّةَ قَريباً؟

after.known: why do you want to learn Arabic soon?

problem: Meaning: the English adds the degree emphasis “so”.
evidence: The Arabic has only قَريباً, “soon”; its sibling phrases also use this for plain “soon”. Removing “so” restores the taught meaning without adding vocabulary.

before.known: because I want to speak more quickly
before.target: لِأَنَّني أُريدُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ أَكْثَرَ بِسُرْعَة

after.known: because I want to speak more with everyone
after.target: لِأَنَّني أُريدُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ أَكْثَرَ مَعَ الجَميعِ

problem: Meaning: “more quickly” expresses speed, not a greater amount of speaking.
evidence: أَكْثَرَ is the amount-of-speaking tile in this group; بِسُرْعَة separately supplies “quickly”. The replacement uses the same group’s established “speak more with everyone” construction and retains أَكْثَرَ.

before.known: because I want to speak Arabic more easily soon
before.target: لِأَنَّني أُريدُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ العَرَبِيَّةَ أَكْثَرَ بِسُهولَة قَريباً

after.known: because I want to speak Arabic easily soon
after.target: لِأَنَّني أُريدُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ العَرَبِيَّةَ بِسُهولَة قَريباً

problem: Meaning/grammar: quantity “more” is being used as an English comparative adverb.
evidence: The siblings distinguish أَكْثَرَ (“more” speaking/learning) from بِسُهولَة (“easily”) and بِسُرْعَة (“quickly”). Appending the latter to أَكْثَرَ does not supply the intended comparative of ease or speed. Remove “more” on both sides; the current LEGO remains intact.

before.known: will you help me?
before.target: هَلْ سَتُساعِدُني؟

evidence: The current practice target adds هَلْ to the other target in this normalised-known group. A contextual prompt using the already practised “this evening” removes this row from that collision while preserving سَتُساعِدُني; the same contextual pair is already a sibling USE.

before.known: because I want to meet many people who speak Arabic
before.target: لِأَنَّني أُريدُ أَنْ أَلْتَقِيَ بِأُناسٍ يَتَكَلَّمونَ العَرَبِيَّةَ كَثيراً

evidence: بِأُناسٍ يَتَكَلَّمونَ العَرَبِيَّةَ كَثيراً puts كَثيراً with speaking, not a count of people. B03 in this group correctly glosses this construction as “people who speak Arabic a lot”.

before.known: I don't like to take too much time, nearly all day
before.target: لا أُحِبُّ أَنْ آخُذَ وَقْتاً كَثيراً تَقْريباً طَوالَ اليَومِ

problem: R8 tier 2: the trailing “nearly all day” has no clear attachment.
evidence: “I don’t like to take too much time, nearly all day” neither builds a natural fragment nor clearly expresses the duration of taking time. The replacement uses the complete, already established sibling U02 construction.

before.known: I don't like to take too much time when speaking with nearly everyone

problem: Meaning: the English inserts an activity absent from the Arabic.
evidence: The target ends مَعَ الجَميعِ تَقْريباً, “with nearly everyone”; there is no speaking verb. B04 uses the matching “take too much time with everyone” construction. Remove the unsupported “when speaking”.

before.known: too much time to answer
before.target: آخُذَ وَقْتاً كَثيراً لِلإِجابَة

after.target: وَقْتاً كَثيراً لِلإِجابَة

problem: Meaning: the target includes “I take”, absent from the English fragment.
evidence: The target begins آخُذَ, the first-person verb used inside the full sibling sentence. The known fragment is just “too much time to answer”. Removing that verb aligns the fragments and preserves لِلإِجابَة.

before.known: I don't like to take too much time to answer with everyone
before.target: لا أُحِبُّ أَنْ آخُذَ وَقْتاً كَثيراً لِلإِجابَة مَعَ الجَميعِ

after.known: I don't like to take too much time to answer today

problem: R8 tier 2: “to answer with everyone” needs an invented group-answering context.
evidence: The seed concerns the time taken to answer, not answering in unison. “With everyone” makes the ordinary reading unclear. The replacement uses the natural same-group B03 sentence and retains the answer tile.

before.known: start talking as soon as possible today
before.target: مِنَ المُفيدِ أَنْ تَبْدَأَ بِالتَّكَلُّمِ في أَقْرَبِ وَقْتٍ مُمْكِن اليَومَ

after.known: it's useful to start talking as soon as possible today

problem: Meaning: the English omits “it’s useful to”.
evidence: The Arabic begins مِنَ المُفيدِ أَنْ تَبْدَأَ, as do the full sibling sentences. The current English instead reads as an imperative or bare verb fragment. Restore the already taught opening.

before.known: but you wanted to speak more before you had to go
before.target: لٰكِنْ أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَتَكَلَّمَ أَكْثَرَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْتَهِيَ

after.known: but you wanted to speak more before it ended

problem: Meaning: “before you had to go” is translated as “before it ended”.
evidence: The target ends قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْتَهِيَ, the established ending/finishing clause also seen in B03. It contains neither necessity nor going. Correct the known side to match that clause.

before.known: how long have you been trying to speak more?
before.target: مُنْذُ مَتى وَأَنْتَ تُريدُ أَنْ تَتَكَلَّمَ أَكْثَرَ؟

after.known: how long have you been wanting to speak more?

problem: Meaning: “trying” is translated as “wanting”.
evidence: The target uses تُريدُ أَنْ تَتَكَلَّمَ, “want to speak”, as in U02, rather than a trying verb. Align the known side with the wanting pattern already used by its siblings.

before.known: he doesn't want to be with everyone as soon as possible

evidence: Unlike the sibling time references today/tonight, “as soon as possible” makes the negative state depend on a contrived rejected scheduling intention. Use the established time word “today” with the same subject and complement.
